questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests multi-tenant isolation, per-tenant DB rotation, and integration with Kubernetes and AppRole. It probes policy scope, TTL planning, and rollback safety.

## Key Concepts
- Vault Enterprise namespaces
- Database secrets engine per-tenant
- AppRole + Kubernetes auth binding
- Lease management and auto-renewal
- Rollback via lease revocation and canary validation

## Code Example
```bash
# Tenant A DB secret engine
vault secrets enable database -path=tenant-A/database
vault write tenant-A/database/roles/tenant-postgres \
  db_name=postgres \
  creation_statements="CREATE USER \"{{name}}\" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '{{password}}';" \
  default_ttl="15m" max_ttl="30m"
# Bind AppRole (example)
vault write auth/approle/role/tenant-A-approle token_ttl=1h token_max_ttl=4h \
  secret_id_ttl=24h
# Kubernetes login binding (example)
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/tenant-A-approle \
  bound_service_account_names=tenant-a-sa \
  bound_service_account_namespaces=tenant-a \
  policies=tenant-a-read \
  ttl=15m
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor and alert on credential rotation failures?
- What changes if TTLs must be dynamically adjusted per-tenant?

## Why This Is Asked
This checks ability to implement tenant isolation via Vault policies and AppRole using KV prefixes, a common beginner pattern.

## Key Concepts
- Policies and least privilege
- KV v2 secrets engine
- AppRole binding
- Token TTL and leases
- Offboarding and audit hygiene

## Code Example
```bash
# Policy: tenant-<id>-pol.hcl
path "secret/tenant-<id>/*" {
  capabilities = ["read"]
}
path "sys/leases/revoke" {
  capabilities = ["update"]
}

# Create policy
vault policy write tenant-<id>-pol tenant-<id>-pol.hcl

# KV v2 mount
vault secrets enable -path=secret/tenant-<id> kv-v2

# AppRole
```
